Rashi on Ketubot 54a:11:1.english: She made her ketubah an apoteiki - [The] land designated for her ketubah, she made [it] an apoteiki [property designated for repayment] for her creditor.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:11:2.hebrew: הני אין - לפי שהן גיבוי כתובה, אבל תביעה לא:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:11:2.english: [In] these [cases], yes - because they are collection of the marriage contract, whereas claiming [is] not.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:14:1.english: Its surrounding towns [parvadaha] - Cities adjacent to it.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:14:2.english: Meḥoza - [It is] one of the surrounding towns of Babylonia.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:15:1.english: Where the kav of Nehardea is current - Any place where they measure grain with the measure of the kav of Nehardea.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:16:1.hebrew: שמין מה שעליה - כשמגבין לה בית דין כתובתה, שמין בגדיה בפרעון כתובה:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:16:1.english: They appraise what is upon her - When the court collects her ketubah for her, they appraise her garments toward the payment of [her] ketubah.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:16:2.hebrew: בלקיט - שכיר שגר בבית בעל הבית ולקח לו בעל הבית בגדים — כשיוצא ממנו, שם אותן בגדים בשכרו לשמואל, ורב אמר: אין שמין:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:16:2.english: With regard to a hired worker - [This refers to] a hired worker who lives in the householder's house and the householder bought clothes for him; when he leaves him, he appraises those clothes toward his wages according to Shmuel, and Rav said: They are not appraised.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:17:1.english: And likewise with regard to a hired worker - According to Rav, one appraises [his garments], and according to Shmuel, one does not appraise [them].

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:17:2.english: And he placed in it - Rav [placed] a mnemonic in his statement.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:17:3.english: An orphan and a widow, strip and go out - Strip off their garments and go out.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:18:1.english: That we learned in a mishna - In this [mishna] of Arakhin.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:18:2.hebrew: אחד המקדיש נכסיו כו' ואחד המעריך עצמו - והגזבר בא למשכנו על ערכו הקצוב בפרשה, אין לו לגזבר לא בכסות אשתו כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:18:2.english: One who consecrates his property, etc., and one who valuates himself - And the [Temple] treasurer comes to exact a pledge from him for his valuation that is fixed in the [Torah] portion; the treasurer has no [claim] on his wife's clothing, etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:18:3.hebrew: לשמן - בגדים שצבע לשם אשתו ולשם בניו, ואע"פ שלא לבשום עדיין. אלמא בגדיה שלה, כשמואל:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:18:3.english: For them - Garments that he dyed for his wife and for his children, even though they have not yet worn them. Thus, her garments belong to her, in accordance with [the opinion of] Shmuel.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:19:1.hebrew: לכאורה כשמואל ריהטא - פתאום מרוצת משמעות המשנה כשמואל, אבל כי מעיינת בה לא מסייעא לשמואל, דהא קמיה קיימא ואינה יוצאה מביתו, ואדעתא דהכי מקני לה שיהו שלה כל זמן שהיא תחתיו:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:19:1.english: At first glance it runs like Shmuel - At first glance, the flow of the Mishnah's meaning is like Shmuel, but when you examine it, it does not support Shmuel, for [the wife] is standing before him and is not leaving his house, and it is with this intention that [her husband] transfers ownership to her, so that [the garments] are hers as long as she is under him.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:1:1.hebrew: כיון דלית לה כתובה - לאם, לית לה מזוני דבת, דהא תנאי כתובה הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:1:1.english: Since she does not have a ketubah - [referring] to the mother, [then] she does not have a daughter's sustenance, for [that] is a stipulation of the ketubah.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:22:1.english: A certain [person] who said to them - [This was] a deathbed will.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:22:2.hebrew: נדוניא לברת - קצובים היו תכשיטי הבנות, כך וכך לבושים:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:22:2.english: A dowry to [my] daughter - The daughters' adornments were fixed [at] such-and-such garments.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:22:3.hebrew: פורנא ליתמי - הריוח ליתומים, ולא אמרינן ניתיב לה דמי הנדוניא כיום הצוואה:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:22:3.english: Purna [goes] to the orphans - The profit [belongs] to the orphans, and we do not say: "Let us give her the value of the dowry as [it was on] the day of the will."

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:2:1.hebrew: בת ארוסה - הבא על ארוסתו וילדה לו, ומת ולו בנים, יש לה מזונות מנכסיו או לא:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:2:1.english: Daughter of a betrothed woman - [This refers to] one who had relations with his betrothed and she bore him [a daughter], and he died leaving sons — does she have [the right to] sustenance from his estate, or not?

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:2:2.hebrew: כיון דאית לה כתובה - כגון שכתב לה מן האירוסין, אי נמי רבנן תקון נמי לארוסה:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:2:2.english: Since she has a marriage contract - For example, where he wrote [one] for her from betrothal, or else [that] the Sages enacted [a marriage contract] for a betrothed woman as well.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:2:3.hebrew: או דלמא כיון דלא תקון רבנן - למכתב עד שעת נשואין, תנאי כתובה נמי מקמי הכי לא חייל:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:2:3.english: Or perhaps, since the Sages did not enact - [a requirement] to write [a marriage contract] until the time of marriage, the stipulation of the marriage contract also does not take effect prior to that.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:3:1.hebrew: בת אנוסה - אנס את הנערה ונשאה אחרי כן, כדכתיב: "ולו תהיה לאשה", וילדה לו בת ומת; יש לה מזונות מן האחין או לא:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:3:1.english: The daughter of a raped woman - [A man] raped a young woman and married her afterward, as it is written: "And she shall be his wife," and she bore him a daughter, and [he] died — does she have [a right to] sustenance from the brothers or not?

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:3:2.english: She has a marriage contract - [Payable] from his property.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:3:3.hebrew: מנה - אם מת, ואע"ג שכבר נתן כסף קנסה לאביה:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:3:3.english: One hundred dinars - If he dies, even though he already gave the money of her fine to her father.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:4:1.english: The money of her fine went toward her ketubah - And she has no ketubah.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:4:2.hebrew: מאי - מזונות הבת, שהן תנאי כתובה, פקעי בהכי או לא? מי אמרינן כיון דלית לה כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:4:2.english: What [is the halakha] - Does the sustenance of the daughter, which is a stipulation of the marriage contract, cease with this, or not? Do we say: since she does not have [a marriage contract], etc.?

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:5:1.hebrew: או דלמא כתובה היינו טעמא - דלא תקון לה רבנן, משום דכל כתובת אשה משום שלא תהא קלה בעיניו להוציאה תקנוה:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:5:1.english: Or perhaps [regarding] a ketubah, this is the reason - that the Rabbis did not enact [one] for her, because every woman's ketubah was enacted so that she would not be demeaned in his eyes [for him] to divorce her.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:5:2.hebrew: והא לא מצי מפיק - כדכתיב "לא יוכל לשלחה". כתובה דמשום אפוקי הוא, דלא תקון דליכא למיחש, לית לה; אבל שאר תנאי כתובה, דלאו משום "שלא תהא קלה" איתקון, אית לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:5:2.english: And this one, he cannot divorce [her] - As it is written, "He may not send her away" [Deuteronomy 22:29]. A marriage contract, which is on account of divorce — which [the Sages] did not enact [for her] since there is no concern [that he will divorce her] — she does not have; however, the other stipulations of a marriage contract, which were not enacted because of "so that she will not be demeaned [in his eyes]," she does have.

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:6:1.hebrew: בביתי ולא בביקתי - אם יש לו בית, כופין את היורשין לתת לה מדור לפי כבודה, ואין יכולין לומר לה: "לכי לבית אביך ואנו זנין אותך שם". אבל אין לו בית אלא ביקתא בעלמא — צריף צר וקטן, ולשון ביקתא: "בי עקתא" (שבת דף עז:) — יכולין לומר: "לכי מאצלנו", ד"את תהא יתבא בביתי" כתב לך, ולא בביקתי:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:6:1.english: In my house, and not in my hovel [bikati] - If he has a house, we compel the heirs to give her a dwelling in accordance with her dignity, and they cannot say to her, "Go to your father's house, and we will sustain you there." But [if] he has no house, only a mere hovel [bikta] — a narrow and small hut, and the meaning of bikta is bei akta [a cramped house] (Shabbat 77b) — they can say [to her], "Go away from us," for [it was] "You shall dwell in my house" [that] he wrote to you, and not "in my hovel."

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:6:2.hebrew: אבל מזוני אית לה - בבית אביה מנכסיו, ולא אמרינן כיון דלא קרינן בה "ואת תהא יתבא בביתי", לא קרינן בה "ומתזנא מנכסי". ורב יוסף "בביתי" יתירא דריש, דתקון למכתב "בביתי" תרי זימני — "ואת תהא יתבא בביתי כל ימי מיגר ארמלותיך בביתי":
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:6:2.english: But she has sustenance - [Even while] in her father's house, from his property, and we do not say [that] since we cannot apply to her "you shall dwell in my house," we [also] cannot apply to her "and be sustained from my property." And Rav Yosef expounds the extra [mention of] "in my house," for they instituted to write "in my house" twice — "and you shall dwell in my house all the days of your widowhood in my house."

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:7:1.english: And she agreed - We no longer apply to her [the ketubah clause of] "the dwelling of your widowhood."

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:7:2.hebrew: הא לא נתפייסה יש לה - בתמיה, ואפילו אין העכבה מחמת כבוד בעלה, אלא שלא היה תובעה הגון לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 54a:7:2.english: [Then if] she had not agreed, she has [sustenance] - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question: even if the reluctance is not out of respect for her [deceased] husband, but rather because the one proposing to her was not suitable for her?

Rashi on Ketubot 54a:8:1.english: She painted [her eyes] and adorned [herself] - She reveals her intention that it is not out of respect for her husband [that] she is refraining from marrying.

Tosafot on Ketubot 54a:10:1.hebrew: לית הלכתא ככל הני שמעתתא - [אכולהו קאי], בר מתבעוה לינשא, דההוא עדיפא; דאי "ככל הני" דוקא, וקאי נמי אתבעוה לינשא, א"כ קשיא דשמואל אדשמואל, לרב ענן דאמר לעיל: "לדידי מפרשא לי מיניה דמר שמואל כו'". וכה"ג איכא בפרק תולין (שבת דף קמ.): "לית הלכתא ככל הני שמעתתא", דלאו דוקא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 54a:10:1.english: The halakha is not in accordance with all these statements - [This refers to all of them] except for [the case where] they proposed to marry her, for that [case] is stronger; for if "all these" were literal, and it also referred to [the case where] they proposed to marry her, then [one statement of] Shmuel would contradict [another statement of] Shmuel, according to Rav Anan who said above: "It was explained to me personally by Mar Shmuel, etc." And similarly, there is [such an expression] in the chapter [entitled] Tolin (Shabbat 140a): "The halakha is not in accordance with all these statements," which is not literal.

Tosafot on Ketubot 54a:13:1.hebrew: ושמואל אמר הלכה כאנשי גליל - פר"ח: ובמקום שיש מנהג, ילכו אחר המנהג; ובמקום שאין מנהג, יעשו כשמואל, דהלכתא כוותיה. והא דבעי בסמוך עד היכן נהרדעא, לאו משום דאין הלכה כשמואל, אלא משום דשאר בבל נהוג כרב. והא דקשה מההיא דאלמנה (לקמן כתובות צה:) — שם אפרש בע"ה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 54a:13:1.english: And Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with the residents of the Galilee - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: And in a place where there is a custom, they should follow the custom; and in a place where there is no custom, they should act in accordance with Shmuel, for the halakha is in accordance with him. And [the reason] that [the Gemara] asks shortly [hereafter], "How far does Nehardea [extend]?" is not because the halakha is not in accordance with Shmuel, but rather because the rest of Babylonia followed the custom of Rav. And as for that which is difficult from that [passage] regarding a widow (below, Ketubot 95b) — there I will explain [it], with God's help.

Tosafot on Ketubot 54a:3:1.hebrew: בת אנוסה מהו - תימה, דאנוסה גופה תיבעי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 54a:3:1.english: What is [the law regarding] the daughter of a raped woman - It is astonishing, for [he] should have asked [about] the raped woman herself:

Tosafot on Ketubot 54a:6:1.hebrew: בביתי ולא בביקתי - כשאין להן כי אם ביקתי, היא מפסדת, דלכולי עלמא יכולין לגרשה. וביש להם בתים טובים, היא מרווחת בהאי לישנא דביתי, שמשתמשת במדור כדרך שנשתמשה בחיי בעלה, כדאמרינן בהנושא (לקמן כתובות דף קג.), ואין להחליף לה לגרוע ממנו, או שמא אפילו לכיוצא בו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 54a:6:1.english: "In my house, and not in my hovel [bikati]" - When they [the heirs] have only a hovel, she loses out, for according to everyone they can expel her [from it]. And when they have good houses, she benefits from this wording of "my house," for she uses the dwelling in the same way she used [it] during her husband's lifetime, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaNosei (below, Ketubot 103a), and they may not exchange [it] for her for one inferior to it, or perhaps even for one similar to it.
